summary: Two Zimbabwean journalists were freed on bail after alleging they were tortured by military interrogators for writing about an army coup attempt against President Robert Mugabe's government.
President Robert Mugabe called on Zimbabwe's highest judges to resign after they questioned his commitment to the rule of law, accusing them of an "outrageous and deliberate act of impudence."
Students at the University of Zimbabwe boycott classes, joining trade unions, human rights groups, and others in declaring opposition to President Robert Mugabe over his rule.
Joshua Nkomo, Zimbabwean nationalist and former vice-president who lost the presidency to Robert Mugabe in 1980, died aged 82.
President Robert Mugabe delivered the chief eulogy at the funeral of his former arch-rival, Vice-President Joshua Nkomo, who was buried at the Heroes' Acre national monument before a crowd of 30,000.
Robert Mugabe pushed through forcible land seizures in Zimbabwe.

Early results indicated overwhelming "No" votes in Zimbabwe's referendum on President Robert Mugabe's proposed constitutional reforms, including prolonging his term and allowing farm seizures without compensation.
Robert Mugabe suffered an unprecedented personal defeat when his referendum on Zimbabwe's new draft constitution was rejected, with less than 12% of the total electorate backing him.
Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe indicated at a Zanu-PF central committee meeting that he will not run for re-election when his term expires in 2002, though he did not state this definitively.

Zimbabwean voters delivered a stinging rebuke to President Robert Mugabe by voting against the seizure of white-owned farms, though Mugabe said he would proceed anyway and postponed elections due that spring.
President Robert Mugabe accuses Britain of treating Zimbabwe like a colony at the opening of an EU-Africa summit in Cairo, responding to British criticism of political violence.
Robin Cook meets with Robert Mugabe in Cairo, where Mugabe gives assurances that may reduce tensions in Zimbabwe.
Robert Mugabe chose not to soften his policies upon returning from abroad, despite some in his government appearing to want him to do so.

President Robert Mugabe describes white landowners as "enemies of our people" in a televised address and signs into law a constitutional amendment allowing the seizure of white-owned farms without compensation.
British multi-millionaire Nicholas Hoogstraten confirms he has been a long-standing financial backer of Robert Mugabe and Zimbabwe's ruling Zanu-PF party since the early 1960s.

A letter recounts that troops from Robert Mugabe's 6th brigade broke into the writer's property, beat their father and left him for dead, and accuses Mugabe of having tens of thousands of Ndebele people killed over the past 18 years.
President Robert Mugabe is expected to set a date for parliamentary elections within days amid political violence and Commonwealth pressure over the rule of law.
President Robert Mugabe called a general election for next month amid worsening state-sponsored political violence and intimidation in Zimbabwe.
Robert Mugabe announces the seizure of 804 mostly white-owned farms for the resettlement of poor black farmers.

Zimbabwe's opposition Movement for Democratic Change is poised to win a majority of contested parliamentary seats in the coming weekend's election, potentially defeating President Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF party.
Opposition leader Eddie Cross predicts Robert Mugabe will be out of power within a month and Morgan Tsvangirai will become Zimbabwe's new president.
Zimbabweans vote in elections that the article hopes will result in an emphatic rejection of President Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF party.
Zimbabwe's ruling Zanu-PF party warns that President Robert Mugabe would defy all calls for his immediate resignation even if weekend election results swung decisively against him.

Opposition supporters in Zimbabwe predict a landslide victory over President Robert Mugabe's ruling Zanu-PF party as high-turnout parliamentary elections are held, with results not expected before late 2000-06-27.
President Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF party wins Zimbabwe's parliamentary elections, defying British critics who had expected the regime to be voted out.
Zimbabwe's white farmers offer 600 farms for sale to President Robert Mugabe's government for redistribution to poor blacks, in a bid to avert the impending seizure of 804 farms.
President Robert Mugabe's government begins widespread seizures of 160 white-owned farms and deploys army units into townships near Harare and other cities that supported the opposition.

Zimbabwe's state news agency reports that President Robert Mugabe is ready to step down at the 2002 presidential election and let a group of kingmakers groom a successor, though his spokesman denies any such group has been formed.
The Zimbabwean government announced it will step up land seizures to immediately take possession of 3,000 white-owned farms, a move directed by President Robert Mugabe.
Zimbabwe opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai calls on President Robert Mugabe to hold early elections or resign, warning of a popular uprising otherwise.
President Robert Mugabe threatens to put former Rhodesian leader Ian Smith on trial for genocide and revokes Zimbabwe's national racial reconciliation policy.
Zimbabwe's opposition Movement for Democratic Change begins impeachment proceedings against President Robert Mugabe, delivering articles of impeachment to the Speaker of Parliament.

Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe's government proceeded with seizures of more than 50 new white-owned farms, defying a Supreme Court ruling that the land occupations were unconstitutional and must stop.

South African President Thabo Mbeki and Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo travel to Harare and publicly criticize Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe for his violent land seizures, failing to persuade him to uphold the rule of law.
Rioting against the government broke out in Harare, with police firing teargas to disperse rioters, amid anger against President Robert Mugabe's leadership as the economic crisis deepened.
Voting opens in Zimbabwe’s Bikita West by-election, marked by illegalities and violence by war veterans supporting Robert Mugabe’s Zanu-PF party.
Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe attends the burial of assassinated Congolese president Laurent Kabila in Kinshasa, where he was greeted by crowds chanting his name.
Zimbabwe's Justice Minister Patrick Chinamasa told Supreme Court judges their safety could not be guaranteed if they did not resign, part of a government campaign against the judiciary.

Robert Mugabe’s government issues expulsion orders against two foreign correspondents in Zimbabwe and is expected to force other foreign correspondents to leave, amid broader actions against political rivals, judges, and media ahead of his presidential re-election bid.
Robert Mugabe marks his 77th birthday with celebrations, including a small party in Harare and a larger bash at Victoria Falls organized by the 21st February Movement.

Robert Mugabe remains firmly in control in Zimbabwe, having neutralized political challenges, forced out the white chief justice, and moved against the judiciary and press ahead of the next presidential election.
At the funeral for murdered white farmer Gloria Olds in southern Zimbabwe, a Presbyterian minister calls down a curse on President Robert Mugabe's government and its officials.

The Commonwealth agrees to send a ministerial mission to Zimbabwe to express concern to President Robert Mugabe over recent attacks on the judiciary and media, a decision Zimbabwe's government rejects as illegal and vows not to cooperate with.
An International Bar Association report warns that rule of law in Zimbabwe is near collapse under President Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF regime, risking anarchy.
Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe cancelled a trip to Indonesia for the G-15 summit following the death of Defence Minister Moven Mahachi in a car accident.
Zimbabwe's government dismissed reports that senior military officers had warned South Africa they may overthrow President Robert Mugabe.

Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe is reported to be escalating a wave of political violence, which has killed 39 Zimbabweans so far this year, in an apparent effort to create a pretext to cancel the March 2002 presidential election.
Zimbabwe and Britain reached an agreement in Abuja committing Zimbabwe to end illegal farm seizures and violence, with Britain pledging £36m toward land reform compensation.

Robert Mugabe faces a roughly one-month deadline to demonstrate Zimbabwe's commitment to the Abuja agreement reached with the Commonwealth, with possible censure or suspension at the forthcoming Commonwealth summit in Brisbane if abuses continue.

The politburo of Zimbabwe's ruling party Zanu-PF unanimously endorses the Commonwealth agreement in which Britain promised money for land redistribution and Robert Mugabe's government promised to restore the rule of law.
Zimbabwe's revamped supreme court issued a temporary ruling upholding President Robert Mugabe's "fast track" seizures of white-owned land.

The Commonwealth mission to Zimbabwe ended by avoiding censuring President Robert Mugabe's government for failing to uphold the rule of law, issuing only a diluted statement urging him to maintain law and order.
Ministers from six Southern African Development Community states endorsed Robert Mugabe’s re-election campaign despite reports of political violence, chaotic land reform, and media repression.

Commonwealth ministers took the first step toward punitive action against Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe over human rights violations, placing possible suspension on the agenda for their next meeting.
Robert Mugabe called a presidential election for early March as his government began forcing through repressive legislation, including new security laws and press curbs.
Zimbabwe's Zanu-PF party, led by Robert Mugabe, used its parliamentary majority to pass two controversial bills designed to stifle dissent ahead of the presidential election.
Britain confirms it will call for Zimbabwe's suspension from the Commonwealth if President Robert Mugabe violates its values.

Commonwealth foreign ministers rebuffed Britain's call to immediately suspend Zimbabwe from meetings and gave President Robert Mugabe a last chance to restore conditions for a free and fair presidential election in March.

Robert Mugabe's government files fresh treason charges against two deputies of opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai, following Tsvangirai's own treason charge for allegedly plotting to assassinate Mugabe.
Robert Mugabe’s government used hired youths, torture camps, food denial, and electoral manipulation to terrorize the population into voting for him in Zimbabwe’s March elections.
An Observer investigation reports that torture camps have been set up in Zimbabwe where suspected opponents of Robert Mugabe are being murdered and mutilated ahead of elections.
Commonwealth leaders decide to delay action against Zimbabwe until after the March 9-10 presidential elections, despite a split over a British proposal to immediately suspend Zimbabwe.
An opinion poll ahead of Zimbabwe's election in three days shows Robert Mugabe with 11.3% support versus Morgan Tsvangirai's 19.8%, while 60% of voters are too afraid to state their choice.
Robert Mugabe spent the final day of his election campaign touring ruling party rural strongholds north of Harare ahead of Zimbabwe's presidential polls.

Zimbabwe's ruling party Zanu-PF raises the prospect of a military coup if President Robert Mugabe loses the weekend election, with party official Didymus Mutasa saying the party would support such a coup.

Zimbabwe holds a presidential election that will determine whether Robert Mugabe extends his 22-year rule, with the opposition Movement for Democratic Change relying on a massive turnout to defeat him.
Robert Mugabe is declared the winner of Zimbabwe's presidential election, after which his forces launch violent retribution and repression against suspected opposition supporters.
President Robert Mugabe wins Zimbabwe's election, securing another six-year term.
Robert Mugabe prepares to be sworn in for another six-year term as president of Zimbabwe amid international condemnation of the violence-scarred elections.
Zimbabwe's Commonwealth membership was suspended for 12 months with immediate effect after a Commonwealth troika ruled on the country's violent presidential election.
Zimbabwe was suspended from the councils of the Commonwealth for one year after international observers condemned the presidential election as unfairly tilted toward Robert Mugabe.
Zimbabwe's trade unions begin a three-day general strike to protest the harassment of pro-opposition workers following Robert Mugabe's victory in the disputed presidential election.
Zimbabwe's opposition will argue in court that Robert Mugabe won the presidential election by massive fraud and violence.

The Economist Intelligence Unit report says Zimbabwe's economy will continue to decline rapidly under President Robert Mugabe's rule, with the economy having shrunk by at least a third and inflation over 100 percent.
President Robert Mugabe's government ordered around 2,900 of Zimbabwe's 4,000 white farmers to stop working on their farms by midnight, as part of the fast-track land seizure programme.
A Zimbabwe court rules that opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai will stand trial in November on charges of plotting to assassinate President Robert Mugabe.
President Robert Mugabe ordered white farmers defying eviction orders to leave Zimbabwe, while saying loyal farmers willing to cooperate would not be left completely landless.
Zimbabwe's parliament considers new legislation to speed up the seizure of white-owned land under Robert Mugabe's land seizure program.
President Robert Mugabe boycotts a Commonwealth "troika" summit on Zimbabwe with the leaders of Nigeria, South Africa, and Australia.
One of President Robert Mugabe's senior ministers, trade minister Samuel Mumbengegwi, flew to Brussels for EU talks after being granted a Belgian visa despite opposition demands that it be rejected.

Zimbabwe opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai disclosed that mediators acting for top government officials floated a proposal for President Robert Mugabe to retire in return for immunity from prosecution, which Tsvangirai rejected.

Zimbabwe's ruling Zanu-PF party denies reports that two leading officials approached opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai with a plan for President Robert Mugabe to step down before his term expires in 2008.
A former RAF flight lieutenant, Paddy Longe, will return a medal presented to him by Robert Mugabe in protest at Mugabe's regime and the decision to stage World Cup cricket matches in Zimbabwe.

Britain's government insists the EU travel ban on Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe and his associates must be upheld by all countries that voted for it, including France, and confirms Britain will seek to extend the ban at a European foreign ministers meeting in Brussels.

EU foreign ministers failed to reach agreement on sanctions against Zimbabwe, with France seeking flexibility so Robert Mugabe could visit Paris while Britain, Germany, Sweden and the Netherlands opposed exempting him from a travel ban.
French President Jacques Chirac brushed aside British objections to his decision to invite Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe to a summit in Paris later in February.
The European Union failed again to agree to renew its sanctions against Zimbabwe, which would still allow President Robert Mugabe to attend a Franco-African summit in Paris.
European Union governments renewed a travel ban on Robert Mugabe and his top officials for a year, but granted him an exemption to attend a summit in Paris.
EU ambassadors postpone the Lisbon summit indefinitely because they cannot find a way to exclude Zimbabwean leader Robert Mugabe, coinciding with the renewal of EU sanctions against his regime.
Human rights activists called on the Commonwealth to investigate abuses by state-sponsored youth militias loyal to President Robert Mugabe in Zimbabwe.
Robert Mugabe attends a two-day Africa summit in Paris after receiving a temporary exemption from European Union sanctions.
A secret government report leaked to a London newsletter reveals that some of President Robert Mugabe's closest allies and relatives seized farms intended for the resettlement of poor blacks.

Investigations by the Guardian reveal allegations that youth militia and groups allied to President Robert Mugabe’s ruling party are using rape as a political weapon against opposition supporters in Zimbabwe.

A confidential Commonwealth report distributed to heads of government accuses Robert Mugabe's government of severe human rights abuses, press and judiciary repression, and responsibility for Zimbabwe's famine.
Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe marked the country's 23rd independence anniversary with an attack on the UK and US for trying to recolonise the country.

Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe faces unprecedented pressure from fellow African leaders, including South African President Thabo Mbeki and Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, who were due in Harare to urge him to end his 23-year rule.
South African and Nigerian presidents plan to fly to Harare to press President Robert Mugabe to retire after 23 years in power.
Tanks moved into Harare's townships and security forces were put on alert in preparation for a week-long national strike and protests against President Robert Mugabe.

President Robert Mugabe's government deployed police and military forces, firing live bullets and teargas to disperse anti-government protests and arresting opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai and several MDC members.
Zimbabwe's opposition Movement for Democratic Change begins a week of marches and strikes intended to unseat President Robert Mugabe after 23 years in power.

Robert Mugabe’s government deployed security forces and ruling-party militia to crush a week of opposition strikes and protests, while opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai was arrested and charged with treason.
President Robert Mugabe threatens to expel UK high commissioner Sir Brian Donnelly from Harare, claiming he aided opposition protests.
African leaders elected Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe as vice-chairman of the African Union's southern African bureau at the organization's summit in Maputo, Mozambique.
Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe is secretly negotiating immunity from prosecution for crimes committed during his 23-year rule as part of a plan to exit power.
President Robert Mugabe holds crisis meetings with his ruling party to determine how to proceed with negotiations with the opposition amid Zimbabwe's escalating economic collapse.
Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe announced the death of his first vice-president, Simon Muzenda, after a long illness.
Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe insisted he would attend the Commonwealth summit, threatening a split within the Commonwealth.
Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo said he would not issue a last-minute invitation to Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe to attend the Commonwealth heads of government meeting in Abuja, Nigeria.
President Robert Mugabe threatened that Zimbabwe may quit the Commonwealth for good after its continued suspension and exclusion from the heads of government meeting in Nigeria.
Robert Mugabe quits the Commonwealth after its suspension of Zimbabwe is extended.
Commonwealth leaders postponed a final decision on how to handle Robert Mugabe’s barred Zimbabwe regime, while Mugabe attacked Tony Blair and threatened to leave the Commonwealth.

President Robert Mugabe threatens to withdraw Zimbabwe from the Commonwealth after his ruling Zanu-PF party voted for a motion to withdraw unless deadlocked talks over Zimbabwe's suspension go his way.
Robert Mugabe withdraws Zimbabwe completely from the Commonwealth after its suspension was extended.
Zimbabwe withdrew its membership from the Commonwealth with immediate effect after Robert Mugabe rejected the group's decision to extend Zimbabwe's suspension.
The Commonwealth decided to continue Zimbabwe's suspension, and President Robert Mugabe threatened to quit the organization.
Robert Mugabe decides to withdraw Zimbabwe from the Commonwealth after leaders in Abuja extended the country's suspension for electoral violence and rigging.
Zimbabwe remains suspended from the Commonwealth under President Robert Mugabe's regime, a decision Tony Blair calls a victory for Commonwealth values.

A senior Zimbabwean Minister admitted that Robert Mugabe's land redistribution policy failed to benefit many poor black farmers, with fewer than half of those allocated seized white-owned farms having taken them up.
A British court rejects an application for a warrant to arrest and extradite Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe on torture charges, citing absolute immunity for heads of state.
Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe did not attend a state funeral due to chest pains, as announced by state broadcasters.
A report by the Zimbabwe Institute reveals that almost every opposition MP has faced violence, intimidation, or jail under Robert Mugabe's government.
President Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF party was accused of using violence to win a parliamentary by-election in which one opposition supporter was shot dead and 50 more were taken to hospital.

Zimbabwe's government, led by Robert Mugabe, backtracks on plans to nationalize all farmland, stating it will honor ownership rights for land bought on the property market and nationalize only land already seized under its land reform program.

President Robert Mugabe's government was accused by the British charity Redress of a widespread, systematic and planned campaign of organised violence and torture to suppress democratic activities, with documented examples of 8,871 human rights violations in 2001-2003.
Eddison Zvobgo, a founder of Zanu-PF who had led internal challenges to Robert Mugabe's autocratic rule, died aged 68.

Zimbabwe's opposition party, the Movement for Democratic Change (MDC), announced it will boycott all future elections until President Robert Mugabe's government changes its electoral system, ends state violence, and repeals repressive media laws.
Robert Mugabe purged seven senior Zanu-PF officials and reprimanded information minister Jonathan Moyo in an effort to quell succession debate.
Zimbabwe's president Robert Mugabe called parliamentary elections for March 31.
Robert Mugabe launched a three-pronged election campaign strategy, including repression and food distribution tactics, ahead of Zimbabwe's parliamentary elections.

A report by the anti-torture group Redress says state torture and violence make free and fair elections in Zimbabwe impossible, criticising President Robert Mugabe's government for failing to arrest and try suspected torturers.
President Robert Mugabe's ruling Zanu-PF party won a majority in Zimbabwe's parliamentary election, which the opposition and Western powers criticized as fraudulent.
Robert Mugabe secured a two-thirds majority in Zimbabwe's elections, likely enabling him to rewrite the constitution to bolster his position before his expected retirement in 2008.
President Robert Mugabe marked Zimbabwe's 25th independence anniversary with a speech attacking the West, defending his land-seizure policy, and declaring a pivot toward Asian powers.
Amnesty International reports that the Zimbabwe government's abuse of human rights activists has not slowed since the March election that extended President Robert Mugabe's power.
Robert Mugabe indicated for the first time that he will retire as president in 2008 when his current term expires.
A senior minister in Robert Mugabe's government admitted for the first time that Zimbabwe's farm seizures are to blame for repeated crop failures.
On his 82nd birthday, Robert Mugabe urges other African leaders to defy former colonial powers and criticizes the British government and the IMF.

Zimbabwe's government invited dispossessed white farmers to apply for 99-year leases to run farms back under a new policy, a move reported as a tacit admission of the failure of Robert Mugabe's land seizures.

Zimbabwean musician Thomas Mapfumo continues his fight for freedom and social justice against Robert Mugabe, having rejected Mugabe as the Zimbabwean dream turned sour in his 1989 album Corruption, with his latest album Rise Up banned from Zimbabwean airwaves.
Zimbabwe's existing currency ceases to be legal tender and is replaced by a new set of bills, a changeover marked by rising tensions and Mugabe's warnings against protests.
Zimbabwean women now have the world's lowest life expectancy at an average of 34 years under Robert Mugabe's rule, according to World Health Organisation figures.
Zimbabwe's ruling party Zanu-PF passes a resolution to harmonize presidential elections with the 2010 parliamentary poll, extending Robert Mugabe's rule until at least 2010.
President Robert Mugabe's regime is poised to allow hundreds of white farmers to return to their land as Zimbabwe faces starvation and economic collapse.
A secret power-sharing plan proposed by exiled Zimbabwean businessmen to remove Robert Mugabe as president, with UN involvement, was documented in a confidential US embassy memo.
The Trades Union Congress calls for a demonstration outside the French embassy to pressure France not to invite Robert Mugabe to the Franco-African summit.
France and Portugal are considering summit invitations to President Robert Mugabe that would weaken the diplomatic isolation of his regime that Britain is trying to maintain.

Robert Mugabe celebrated his 83rd birthday with a lavish feast for the ruling elite while ordinary Zimbabweans faced empty shops, and Vice-President Joice Mujuru stayed away amid accusations she was plotting to oust him.
Robert Mugabe joined celebrations in Accra marking Ghana's 50th anniversary of independence.
Zimbabwean opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai and others were beaten and tortured in a violent crackdown, which the UK holds Robert Mugabe and his government responsible for.

President Robert Mugabe threatened to expel Western diplomats and warned that police would "hit harder" against opposition demonstrations, admitting members of his own Zanu-PF party were plotting against him.
Robert Mugabe may scrap plans to delay next year's presidential elections and has partially lifted a ban on political protests in Harare's townships, according to his mouthpiece newspaper.
Robert Mugabe was due to arrive in Tanzania for a Southern African Development Community summit where he was expected to face fresh pressure over his crackdown on political opponents.
Robert Mugabe confronts neighbouring leaders at a Southern African Development Community summit in Dar-es-Salaam, Tanzania, amid calls for his retirement.

Zimbabwe's security forces detained opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai and other political activists as President Robert Mugabe prepared to tell southern African leaders that his rule has not degenerated into lawless banditry.
Zimbabwe's Zanu-PF central committee voted to endorse Robert Mugabe as its candidate in the next year's presidential election, rejecting his proposal to delay the election until 2010.
Portugal is prepared to invite President Robert Mugabe of Zimbabwe to a European-African summit in Lisbon in December despite an EU travel ban and sanctions.

President Robert Mugabe opened Zimbabwe's parliament with plans to push through laws allowing him to appoint his successor without an election and requiring businesses to give a controlling stake to ruling party loyalists.
Zimbabwe's president Robert Mugabe received a rapturous welcome from fellow southern African leaders at a regional summit that will discuss the crisis in his country.
Pope accepts Zimbabwe archbishop Pius Ncube's resignation after Robert Mugabe's secret police filmed him in an apparent sexual affair, a move widely seen as silencing Mugabe's most strident critic.
Zimbabwe's parliament began debating a constitutional change that would permit President Robert Mugabe to appoint his successor without holding a general election.
Speculation grows about a possible palace coup within Zanu-PF to remove Robert Mugabe as Zimbabwe's president, though no coup is reported to have occurred.
Gordon Brown has lost his campaign to prevent President Robert Mugabe from attending a Europe-Africa summit in Portugal in December despite the EU travel ban on the Zimbabwean strongman.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel says Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe is entitled to attend a Europe-Africa summit in December, putting her at odds with Gordon Brown, who has threatened to boycott the talks if Mugabe attends.

Ian Smith, the former Rhodesian prime minister, dies at 88; he had described Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe as "mentally deranged" in a 2000 interview, prompting Mugabe to threaten him with arrest.
Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe announced he will travel to Europe to attend an EU-Africa summit in Lisbon, prompting UK Prime Minister Gordon Brown to confirm he will boycott the summit.
Robert Mugabe declared that a "sinister" campaign to bar him from the European-African summit in Lisbon had failed, following support for his attendance.

Robert Mugabe attends the European Union-Africa summit in Lisbon, where Peter Tatchell argues he should be arrested for human rights abuses, though Mugabe enjoys diplomatic immunity as a serving head of state.
Robert Mugabe was nominated by his party as its candidate in the presidential elections next March.
Zimbabwe's police and army chiefs warn they will not allow Robert Mugabe to be defeated in the upcoming presidential election by opposition candidates they deride as puppets and sell-outs to Britain.
Zimbabweans must ask how Robert Mugabe has stayed in power for 28 years and how much longer he can continue as the country approaches another election.
Robert Mugabe is running for re-election after 28 years in power amid a dire economic crisis and falling support, facing opposition from Simba Makoni and Morgan Tsvangirai.
Robert Mugabe was so rocked by the scale of his defeat in Zimbabwe's election that he disappeared from public view and reportedly considered standing down.
Zimbabweans are scheduled to go to the polls in the nation's most hotly contested election since independence in 1980, with Robert Mugabe seeking a sixth term.

Robert Mugabe’s security cabinet met and decided to block the opposition from taking power after elections, with Mugabe favoring declaring himself president again but being persuaded to use the electoral commission to keep the opposition from power.
Zimbabwe will need an election runoff between Robert Mugabe and Morgan Tsvangirai to settle the question of who will fill the office of president of Zimbabwe in 2008.

Robert Mugabe's ruling Zanu-PF party lost control of parliament to the opposition Movement for Democratic Change for the first time since independence, while the presidential election result remained unreleased.

Zimbabwe's opposition Movement for Democratic Change announced that Morgan Tsvangirai had won enough votes to defeat Robert Mugabe outright in the presidential election, while official results remained unannounced.

Robert Mugabe is scheduled to chair a Zanu-PF politburo meeting to discuss the political crisis after the opposition claimed victory in the presidential election and Zanu-PF lost control of parliament.
A government spokesman says Robert Mugabe is ready for a runoff in Zimbabwe's presidential election, quashing opposition hopes he will concede defeat.
War veterans Happy Mariri and Ishmael Dube, who once fought alongside Robert Mugabe, now lead the Zimbabwe Liberators Platform opposing his continued rule.
Robert Mugabe refused to concede defeat after Zimbabwe's election and prepared for a run-off, while the opposition MDC claimed Morgan Tsvangirai had won the presidential vote.

Robert Mugabe’s aides told Zimbabwe’s opposition leaders that he is prepared to give up power in return for guarantees, including immunity from prosecution for past crimes, while warning that if the Movement for Democratic Change does not agree he threatens to declare emergency rule and force another presidential election in 90 days.

Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF party demanded a recount of the presidential election and white cattle ranchers were forced off their land as he fought on political and intimidation fronts after losing control of parliament.

Robert Mugabe, shaken by his defeat in the March 29 presidential election, is mustering all means at his disposal, including violent press-ganging of voters, to win a second-round presidential election run-off, though analysts suggest the Mugabe era is inexorably drawing to a close.

Robert Mugabe is described as having turned against white people who supported Zimbabwe’s independence, including the author’s uncle Guy Clutton-Brock, whose ashes Mugabe had carried back to Zimbabwe in 1995.
Zimbabwe's opposition accuses Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF of using an election recount and delays to fraudulently overturn its defeat while widening a campaign of violent intimidation in rural areas.
Robert Mugabe denounced Britain as "thieving neo-colonialists" in a speech marking Zimbabwe's 28th independence anniversary, his first major appearance since disputed elections.

Zimbabwe's state-run press proposes that Robert Mugabe annul the presidential election and form a national unity government with himself remaining president while a new constitution is negotiated and a fresh ballot held.

Zimbabwe's state-run press floated a proposal for Robert Mugabe to annul the presidential election and form a national unity government with himself as president while a new constitution is negotiated and a fresh ballot held.
A partial recount of Zimbabwe's 29 March election results failed to overturn any original results, leaving Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF party unable to regain control of parliament.
Leaders of Zimbabwe's rival opposition factions reunited to claim control of a parliamentary majority and demand that President Robert Mugabe step down.
A government source said a recount of Zimbabwe's presidential vote showed Robert Mugabe lost to Morgan Tsvangirai but that neither won an outright majority.

Zimbabwe's election commission confirmed that President Robert Mugabe lost the election held five weeks earlier, but that opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai fell below the 50% threshold required to avoid a run-off ballot.

Officials from Zimbabwe's ruling Zanu-PF party say President Robert Mugabe will take part in a run-off presidential election after the electoral commission confirmed he lost the first round but that opponent Morgan Tsvangirai gained less than the 50% needed to avoid a second ballot.
Zimbabwe's ruling party says a second round of presidential elections between Robert Mugabe and Morgan Tsvangirai could be delayed by up to a year.
Morgan Tsvangirai announced he will return to Zimbabwe to contest a presidential run-off against President Robert Mugabe, conditional on international observers and media having full access.
Morgan Tsvangirai is expected to return to Zimbabwe to contest a runoff election against President Robert Mugabe.
Zimbabwean authorities extended the deadline for the presidential election run-off between Robert Mugabe and Morgan Tsvangirai to be held by July 31.
Zimbabwe's electoral commission sets June 27, 2008 as the date for the presidential election run-off between President Robert Mugabe and opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai.
Zimbabwe's army chief Major General Martin Chedondo told soldiers they must leave the military if they do not vote for President Robert Mugabe in next month's run-off poll.
Robert Mugabe made a surprise appearance at a UN world food summit in Rome, drawing fierce criticism from the British government, which accused him of causing Zimbabwe's food crisis.
Robert Mugabe attends a UN global food summit in Rome, avoiding an EU travel ban, drawing condemnation from Downing Street.
The Zimbabwean government banned opposition presidential candidate Morgan Tsvangirai from holding political rallies three weeks ahead of his run-off election against Robert Mugabe.

Robert Mugabe and his generals are described as fighting together in a deadly battle for survival, with Mugabe firmly in place as head of a military junta, following Zanu-PF's loss in the March 29 elections.
Robert Mugabe threatened to arrest opposition leaders he accused of supporting election violence.

Robert Mugabe’s militia and Zanu-PF supporters are reported to have carried out violence, including rape, torture, abductions, killings, and home burnings, in Harare townships such as Epworth ahead of a presidential run-off election.
Zimbabwe opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai pulls out of the presidential run-off against Robert Mugabe, calling it a violent, illegitimate sham.

The UN Security Council unanimously adopts a statement condemning Robert Mugabe's government's "campaign of violence" in Zimbabwe after opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai withdrew from the presidential run-off and sought refuge in the Dutch embassy.
Robert Mugabe rejected regional and international pressure to call off Friday's presidential election, stating the election would proceed.
Robert Mugabe is expected to be sworn in as President of Zimbabwe again after a widely criticized presidential run-off election.
Robert Mugabe was sworn in for a sixth term as Zimbabwe's president after a widely discredited runoff election marked by violence and intimidation.

President George W. Bush orders officials to draw up possible sanctions against Zimbabwe and condemns Robert Mugabe's "blatant disregard" for democracy following a widely condemned presidential election run-off.
Robert Mugabe was sworn in as president of Zimbabwe after being declared the winner of a discredited runoff election.
Robert Mugabe attends the African Union summit in Egypt despite international criticism of his regime, with the AU unlikely to impose harsh punishment or intervention.

Zimbabwe opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai ruled out joining an African Union-called power-sharing government with President Robert Mugabe, saying negotiations should instead lay the ground for a new constitution and fresh elections.

Robert Mugabe and Morgan Tsvangirai are both to attend a signing in Harare of a memorandum of understanding mediated by South African President Thabo Mbeki, outlining a framework for a formal power-sharing agreement to resolve Zimbabwe's political and economic crisis.
Talks began in South Africa between Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF and the Movement for Democratic Change, which Mugabe is using as a time-wasting ploy to retain or extend power.
Talks to resolve Zimbabwe's political crisis were on the brink of collapse as Robert Mugabe refused to surrender control of the government despite losing the last credible election.
A power-sharing deal between Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF and the opposition Movement for Democratic Change, which would leave Mugabe in power with a downgraded presidency, is expected to be sealed soon.
Robert Mugabe refused to surrender control of the government during deadlocked talks to resolve Zimbabwe's political crisis, despite losing the country's last credible election.
Morgan Tsvangirai is detained by Zimbabwean security forces at Harare airport amid power-sharing negotiations involving Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF.

Zimbabwe's main opposition party struck a blow against President Robert Mugabe when its candidate, Lovemore Moyo, was elected parliamentary speaker, marking the first time the opposition has held the position since independence in 1980.
President Robert Mugabe opened Zimbabwe's parliament and was met with boos, jeers, and waving fists from opposition MPs, who refused to stand on his arrival.
Robert Mugabe opened Zimbabwe's parliament, where opposition MPs heckled and protested over the failure to reach a power-sharing deal.
Mugabe said he would form a new government of national unity if Tsvangirai did not sign the power-sharing document.
